subject: Systematic improvement of the likelihood with founder event?

messages.author: 17908c3cf4600a9a
messages.subject: Systematic improvement of the likelihood with founder event?
parts:
Hi Nick and all,

I am experiencing a major likelihood improvement when founder event is added to the Biogeographical model (with whatever the method) with my dataset.
It is also the case with the Psychotria dataset.

I was wondering if any of you has already tested a dataset for which the founder event did not improved the likelihood?


Cheers!


Julien

Hi Julien,

I've used BioGeoBears on a butterflyfish dataset so far and found that DEC fit better (though not significantly) than DEC + J. For the same dataset I also did a BayArea analysis, and in that case BayArea +J fit better than BayArea. We're still in the process of making sense of these results, but I'm attaching the output statistics if you would like have to have a look. I hope this helps!

All the best,
Mericien

messages.author: f989c45ee5541397
messages.subject: Re: Systematic improvement of the likelihood with founder event?
parts:
Hi Julien and others,

Months later than your post, but some observations from working on 4 separate plant groups. DECj is significantly better than DEC on (1) Hawaiian lobeliads, (2) pantropical and post-continental splitting Rinorea of violet family, and (3) world-wide distributed order Brassicales. DECj is NOT significantly better (nor DIVALIKEj) for California Floristic Province Clarkia of evening primrose family. The genera have many overlapping species distributions and have been argued by Raven, Lewis, Stebbins etc. to have primary speciation via allopatry or by isolation of once more widespread gene pools (catastrophic speciation). Thus, likely not demonstrating a lot of dispersal jump mediated speciation. BAYAREALIKEj is the only one of the three that shows significance with the "j" parameter.

Ken

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Systematic improvement of the likelihood with founder event?
parts:
This is very interesting, and thank you for sharing! In
chapter 3 of my Ph.D., I compared two groups of clades,
island and non-island. It appeared that j was typically
lower in non-island clades, but sample size was small
(although statistically significant).

An important criticism of this is that "j" (and "d", "e",
etc.), are not really strictly comparable between different
geographies, e.g. a 3-area system, 4-area system, 5-area
system, etc. Each of these has a different number of
possible events of various types, so the parameters mean
somewhat different things.

However, we would really like to be able to compare between
analyses, since it would be interesting if (for example)
founder-event speciation is important on islands but less so
on continents. The best ideas I've had are:

(1) rather than compare j, compare AICc differences between
DEC and DEC+J (but this is influenced by e.g. phylogeny
size; bigger phylogenies will have more power to distinguish
models).

(2) do stochastic mapping under the inferred model
parameters. Then one could get estimated counts of each
type of event per million years of branch length.

The only problem I can see with #2 is that I have to program
it for the biogeographic models (regular stochstic mapping
with a standard character isn't really the same thing),
which I plan to do hopefully within a month or two.

(another issue would be SSE considerations, also on my radar
but further off)

But, comparing different analyses is a complex question, if
anyone has ideas or criticisms, let me know!

Cheers,
Nick
